label: attack-50-graveyard_attacker
system:
You are one member of a red team. You have been given ONE attack surface and you may not stray from it. You have not seen the author's reasoning and you do not want to; you see only the idea and the evidence.

Your job is to kill the idea on your surface. A weak attack wastes everyone's time. If your surface genuinely does not apply, say so with verdict "abstain" rather than inventing a weak objection; an abstention is not a survival.

Output JSON only.
user:
YOUR SURFACE — graveyard_attacker:
This already died. Find the closest dead product and argue the cause of death has not been dissolved.

IDEA
{
  "id": 50,
  "title": "Who Gave It",
  "unlock": "A spoken entry costs about a cent a minute and can be transcribed and attributed on the handset itself at no marginal cost, and a Live Activity can be started remotely and answered in place rather than firing once into a notification list",
  "pain": "Siblings who each give some of an elderly parent's daily doses have apps that log that a dose was taken but not who gave it, so they re-ask each other in the family group chat and risk double-dosing, using the chat itself as the audit trail [210].",
  "audience": "adult siblings sharing hands-on daily care of one elderly parent in that parent's own home",
  "mechanic": "shared_ledger",
  "wedge": "One medication and one household: you say 'I gave Mum the eight o'clock one' out loud as you do it, your name goes on it, and any later correction is written as a new spoken line with your voice on it rather than quietly replacing what the record already said",
  "moat": "switching_cost_of_history",
  "model": "subscription",
  "loop": "invite_for_function",
  "kill": [
    "Fewer than 60% of households add a second sibling within 14 days - a one-writer ledger is just another pillbox app",
    "Self-reported duplicate-dose questions in the family chat do not fall by at least half by day 30",
    "More than 25% of entries are typed rather than spoken by month 2, meaning the voice is not what kept them",
    "Households drop below 40% retention at month 3, repeating the retention wall that killed a validated medication manager"
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "Everyone's first suggestion here is a shared checklist, which is exactly what the existing apps are and exactly what loses the who - and a checkbox anyone can silently untick is the same hole the commitment-device evidence describes.",
  "why_now": "Attributing a spoken line to the person who said it now costs effectively nothing on the handset, which is the one thing the family group chat was standing in for."
}



Return JSON:
{
  "surface": "graveyard_attacker",
  "attack": "your strongest specific argument, 2-4 sentences, concrete",
  "strongest_defence": "the best answer the author could give",
  "verdict": "fatal" | "wounded" | "survived" | "abstain",
  "verdict_reason": "one sentence"
}

Use "fatal" only when the defence cannot work at all, because a fatal verdict
kills the idea outright and no other score overrides it. Use "wounded" when the
idea survives but is materially weaker. Use "survived" when your surface is
genuinely well answered.
